text:
carla: P0 from customer: after a failover to secondary CloudHSM cluster, ephemeral key signatures started failing verification. This is affecting short-lived token issuance for payments. Ticket #INC-2026. Need owners.
ben: Can you paste the API error and the CloudHSM cluster/partition IDs?
carla: Error from our token service when calling /sign: {
  "error": "SignatureVerificationFailed",
  "code": 403,
  "detail": "key handle lookup failed"
}  Ticket notes: failover happened ~2025-11-02T03:12:08Z. Cluster ARN arn:aws:cloudhsm:us-west-2:12345:cluster:cl-abcde, partition id p1.
eng-hsm-bot: alert: cloudhsm-cluster-cl-abcde detected node failover at 2025-11-02T03:12:07Z :warning:
carla: Repro steps customer shared: 1) call /token/create 2) HSM generates ephemeral key and returns handle 3) downstream service calls /sign with handle -> 403. Happens intermittently after failover.
ben: Ok. Need logs from the HSM proxy and the device audit logs around failover. Also want the output of our internal key map for the handle. Can you run: ```kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-hsm-proxy --since=2h``` and paste the segment around 03:12 UTC?
dima: Also run `aws cloudhsm describe-clusters --cluster-ids cl-abcde` and `sudo /opt/cloudhsm/bin/list_keys -p 1` on the HSM nodes if you can access them. We need to know if ephemeral key material replicated to the secondary partition.
carla: Pasted proxy log snippet: ```2025-11-02T03:11:59Z INFO handle=0x7f3a created ephemeral key id=eph-9a3
2025-11-02T03:12:07Z WARN cluster=cl-abcde node=node-2 failover triggered
2025-11-02T03:12:10Z ERROR handle_lookup handle=0x7f3a not found```.
ella: Did the customer run any HSM key material exports or rotations around that window? If keys were marked no-export we can't move them.
carla: Customer says no manual rotations. They do short retention for these ephemerals (TTL 5m).
carmen: From a compliance side we need the audit entries for the verify operations and any key creation events. Ask them to provide the audit S3 path or we can pull via our audit ingestion. Also note: do not delete keys or logs.
audit-bot: audit files available: s3://redwood-audit/prod/cloudhsm/cl-abcde/2025/11/02/03/audit-logs.gz :eyes:
carla: Uploaded the relevant gzip to the ticket. Snippet shows entries: `CRYPTO_OP CREATE KEY id=eph-9a3` then later `CRYPTO_OP VERIFY FAIL handle=0x7f3a`.
dima: That indicates the HSM returned a handle that later couldn't be resolved on the secondary. Two likely causes: 1) replication lag / in-flight state lost during failover, or 2) keys created with attributes that prevent replication (e.g., partition-local or no-export with missing wrapping).
ben: We should check our wrapping flow. Are ephemerals wrapped by a CMK in KMS before being recorded in the key map? If the wrapping key is KMS-backed and the KMS-to-HSM wrapping didn't complete prior to failover, the secondary won't have unwrapped material.
carla: Customer uses our default flow: generate key inside HSM and store handle reference in Redis. We do not export raw material out of HSM.
ben: That is risky across multi-node HSM failovers: ephemeral keys created on one partition may not be present on another if the cluster is misconfigured or replication stalls. Recommend failing back to primary and validating replication status, then re-creating ephemeral keys or re-issuing tokens.
dima: For immediate diagnostics: we need (a) device serial numbers for all nodes in cl-abcde, (b) partition ID and `list_keys` output from each node, (c) `hsmcli` logs around 03:12, (d) the exact client call payload that created eph-9a3.
carla: Provided device serials and the client payload (sanitized). Also ran `list_keys` on node-1 shows the ephemeral key present; node-2 shows no entry.
carmen: That matches a replication gap. From compliance: confirm that audit logs include key creation and verify entries before any key re-creation — we need immutable trail for SOC.
ben: Short term mitigation: 1) stop issuing new tokens tied to ephemeral handles until we stabilize, 2) if the customer can accept, re-issue tokens by re-creating keys on the active node and inform them of token revocation, 3) open a vendor escalation with AWS CloudHSM to investigate replication/cluster health.
dima: AWS case created: CASE-789102. Include the node logs and audit bundle. Also ask AWS if they have any known replication bug for the agent version.
carla: Customer asks for a safe rewrap procedure that doesn't violate no-export constraints. They cannot export private key material.
ben: If keys were created with no-export, you cannot move raw key material. Two safe options: - Recreate ephemeral keys on the current active HSM and rotate consumers to new handles (recommended). - If you must preserve tokens, implement a short-lived proxy on primary to serve sign ops until you complete a controlled failback and replication verification.
carmen: Compliance note: before any deletion or rotation, create an immutable snapshot of relevant audit logs and tag the ticket. Do not purge S3 audit files.
dima: Repro steps for ENG: 1) Deploy a small load that creates ephemerals and immediately call sign across a simulated failover. 2) Observe handle lookup failures if replication is delayed. 3) Run `sudo /opt/cloudhsm/bin/list_keys -p <partition>` on both nodes before and after failover. Capture times.
carla: I've scheduled a call with the customer and AWS for 2025-11-02T17:00Z. Owners: @dima (eng-hsm), @ben (eng-platform), @carla (support), @carmen (security).
ben: I'll prepare a short runbook: check list_keys parity, audit entries, do controlled replay, escalate to AWS if parity fails.
carla: Customer agreed to pause issuance and will accept reissue. Marking interim workaround accepted.
eng-hsm-bot: note: runbook created at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hsm-ephemeral-replication
audit-bot: reminder: do not delete audit bundles for incidents until closure.
carla: Thanks team. Next steps captured in INC-2026. :thumbsup:
